description: This dataset gives material quantities, embodied greenhouse gas emissions and structural drawings for three structural designs of a 15-storey building, used to show how plan irregularity raises the embodied emissions of tall building structures. It was published on the University of Melbourne's figshare repository (version 3, 3 July 2022) by James Helal, Alireza Mehdipanah, André Stephan, Elisa Lumantarna and Robert Crawford. The three finite element models, regular, moderately irregular and highly irregular, use reinforced concrete shear walls with a moment-resisting frame of band beams, columns and one-way slabs; only the eccentricity of the shear walls changes, so its effect is isolated. Emissions are quantified with a hybrid life cycle inventory method. Files are one calculation workbook per model, a workbook of design loads and considerations and a PDF of structural drawings. Coverage: one 15-storey building scenario. Access: University of Melbourne figshare. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: a hypothetical design; the Australian setting is inferred from the university. Simulation uses: embodied carbon trade-offs in structural design optimisation. Related records: the Finnish residential material inventory and the material stock maps.
